$comment: Starter sheets. Each one is a real sheet.json (schema 1) with placeholder ids that the app
re-mints per sheet, so two sheets made from one template never share a cell key.
Agent columns ship with harness_id: "" on purpose. A template cannot know which agents a
workspace has, and inventing an id would silently run the wrong agent — the app opens that
column's settings on first load and asks which one to use.
`brief` is what the agent is told about the template on the first turn. It is style and
intent, not schema: the schema lives in the sheet-design skill, where it costs nothing per
turn and applies to every turn rather than only the first.

templates.name: Competitor scan
templates.description: One row per company; an agent reads each site and a second one scores the overlap.
templates.brief: A research pipeline read left to right: the person fills in the company and its site, one agent writes a short brief from the site, and a second agent judges how directly it competes. Keep the agent answers to a couple of sentences each.

harness.prompt: Read {{Site}} and write a three-sentence brief on {{Company}}: what they sell, who they sell it to, and how they price it. Put your full notes in notes.md.

Score 1-5 how directly this company competes with us, then one line of why.

{{Brief}}

templates.name: Inbound triage
templates.description: Paste a batch of requests; an agent summarises each one and suggests the next step.
templates.brief: A triage list. The person pastes raw inbound text one row at a time; one agent turns each into a one-line summary plus a suggested next step, and a Stage column tracks what happened. Keep it to two columns of agent work at most.

templates.name: Reading list
templates.description: Links in, summaries out — no agent column until you add one.
templates.brief: A plain working list: a link, why it matters, and a status. No agent columns — this one is for someone who wants to get material in first and decide later what to run over it.
